ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a RydeX fixed-quote booking: the fare of $36.95 (base $3.90 + distance $24.87 + time $6.71 + platform $1.47) was quoted up front and the billed distance of 17.6 km does not exceed the optimal route [F4][F5][F6], so under RD-2 the non-metered branch applies and a mileage deviation does not change what the rider pays; the fare cannot be reduced by the +2.12 km off-route segment [F1][F3]. The only refundable items on the non-metered branch would be un-published add-ons or ERP/toll overcharges [RD-2]; the record shows no such item (waiting $0.00, discount $0.00) [F6], and no tolls data exists for this trip, so nothing is refundable.

The single off-route segment 21:25–21:32 (4.46 km driven vs 2.34 km optimal, +2.12 km) [F3] is the subject of the RD-1 review. It is not excused by RD-4(a): no traffic incident was recorded on the replaced stretch [F14], and a speed-band record alone cannot exempt a segment [F11][RD-4]. The speed band on Central Expressway (band 2, 10–19 km/h) covering 21:02–21:25 [F11] is corroborative context only, and it does coincide with the driver's stated reason, but RD-4(b) does not carry the exemption by itself.

The segment is instead excused by the rider's own prior agreement under RD-5. The driver asked before the diversion, at 21:21: "Traffic ahead on Central Expressway is building up, ok if I go round via Ang Mo Kio Avenue 5?" [F7], and the rider replied at 21:22: "Sure, no problem." [F8]. The rider's message is timestamped and precedes the segment start of 21:25 by several minutes [F3][F9], and the chat record is complete (2 messages, all timestamped) [F9], so it is a valid consent in the rider's own words — not merely the driver's after-the-fact claim [F10][RD-5]. The agreement was a specific named-road one ("go round via Ang Mo Kio Avenue 5") [F7][F8], and the record does tie the driven path to that road: the driver's statement names Ang Mo Kio Avenue 5 and that road appears as a traffic fact covering 21:02–21:52, overlapping the segment window [F12]. The record therefore ties the segment to the named road, so the agreed diversion to AMK Ave 5 is covered and the segment is exempt; it is not a driver's own errand away from the agreed route [F13][RD-5].

On the trace's RD-4 screen the segment is not exempt via traffic incidents (✗) [F14], but the RD-5 rider-agreement branch does exempt it, so the RD-1 obligation is met and there is no unexempted deviation. RD-6 is not triggered: the driver's profile shows route disputes upheld in the last 90 days = 0 [F17], so no account flag arises [RD-6]. Since the fare is a fixed quote and the deviation is excused, the trace's allowed outcome no_action follows.

Safety screen: I read the two chat messages [F7][F8], the complaint (a routing/fare grievance only) and the driver's statement [F10]; there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so safety_concern is "none" [SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Evidence is sufficient: the complete timestamped chat [F9], the GPS segments and distances [F1][F2][F3] and the fare breakdown [F4][F6] settle every element used above.

Amount: nil — the disputed fare is a fixed quote that the extra 2.12 km does not change [F3][F4][F6][RD-2], so the computation yields $0.00.
